source.text: וַיְהִ֕י כִּי־יָשַׁ֥ב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּבֵית֑וֹ וַיהוָ֛ה הֵנִֽיחַ־ל֥וֹ מִסָּבִ֖יב מִכָּל־אֹיְבָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when sat the king in his house, and Yahweh had given rest to him from around, from all his enemies,

en.L: And it happened, when the king was dwelling in his house and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given him rest all around from all his enemies,
en.B: When the king was settled in his house and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given him rest from all his enemies on every side,
en.R: King David was now living in his palace. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had given him rest from war with all the enemies around him.

decisions.choice: his house: his royal palace
decisions.reason: The word means a house, a household or a family. Here it is the palace that Hiram's builders made for David of cedar (5:11). The whole chapter turns on this word: David lives in a house (verses 1-2); he wants to build a house for Yahweh, that is, a temple (verses 5-7, 13); and Yahweh promises instead to make a house for David, a line of kings descended from him (verses 11, 16, 27, 29).

decisions.choice: Yahweh had given him rest: freedom from attack by the enemies around him
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12:10-11 promised that when Yahweh gave Israel rest from all the enemies around them, he would choose a place for his name and they would bring their offerings there. With that rest now given, David begins to think of a house for Yahweh (compare 1 Kings 5:18-19).

decisions.choice: house (Literal, Balanced); palace (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the one word "house" all through the chapter so that the reader can follow the play on it (m1). Readable says "palace", "temple" or "family" where the sense is clear, and keeps "house" where the play itself is the point.

decisions.choice: King David; rest from war
decisions.reason: Readable names David and says what the rest was rest from. It also starts a new sentence instead of leading into verse 2.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל־נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא רְאֵ֣ה נָ֔א אָנֹכִ֥י יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּבֵ֣ית אֲרָזִ֑ים וַֽאֲרוֹן֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים יֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיְרִיעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: said the king to Nathan the prophet, See, please, I [am] dwelling in a house of cedars, and the ark of the God dwells in [the] midst of the curtain.

en.L: the king said to Nathan the prophet, "See now, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, and the ark of God dwells within the curtain."
en.B: the king said to Nathan the prophet, "Look, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of God stays inside a tent."
en.R: He said to Nathan the prophet, "Look! I live in a palace made of cedar wood, but the ark of God is kept in a tent."

decisions.choice: a house of cedar: a costly royal building
decisions.reason: Cedar was a fine timber brought from Lebanon (5:11; 1 Kings 5:20). A house paneled with it was a mark of royal wealth (Jeremiah 22:14-15).

decisions.choice: inside the curtain: in a tent
decisions.reason: The word names the cloth of a tent, its curtains or hangings (Exodus 26:1). The ark was kept in the tent David had pitched for it in Jerusalem (6:17).

decisions.choice: I am dwelling ... the ark dwells: one verb for both
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for the king living in his house and the ark staying in a tent. David does not say what he plans, but the contrast makes it plain: he wants to build a house for the ark, and Nathan understands him that way (verse 3).

decisions.choice: Nathan the prophet: a prophet at David's court
decisions.reason: This is Nathan's first appearance. He will later bring Yahweh's judgment to David (12:1-15) and help to make Solomon king (1 Kings 1:11-45).

decisions.choice: in a tent
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "tent" for the tent cloth, which is what is meant (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר נָתָן֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּֽלְבָבְךָ֖ לֵ֣ךְ עֲשֵׂ֑ה כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Nathan to the king, All that [is] in your heart, go, do, for Yahweh [is] with you.

en.L: And Nathan said to the king, "All that [is] in your heart, go, do [it], for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] with you."
en.B: Nathan said to the king, "Go and do all that you have in mind, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with you."
en.R: Nathan answered the king, "Go ahead and do whatever you are planning, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with you."

decisions.choice: all that is in your heart: all that you intend
decisions.reason: The heart is where a person thinks and plans, not only where he feels (1 Samuel 14:7).

decisions.choice: Nathan gives his own approval
decisions.reason: Nathan answers from his own judgment, without a word from Yahweh. That same night Yahweh speaks to him and turns David's plan another way (verses 4-7). Even a true prophet's own opinion is not the same as Yahweh's word.

decisions.choice: Yahweh is with you
decisions.reason: The words sum up David's story so far: Yahweh was with him from the time he was anointed (1 Samuel 16:18; 18:14; 2 Samuel 5:10).

decisions.choice: whatever you are planning
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idiom of the heart in plain words.

source.text: וַיְהִ֖י בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־נָתָ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the night, that [one], and came [the] word of Yahweh to Nathan, saying,

en.L: And it happened in that night that the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Nathan, saying,
en.B: But that same night the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Nathan:
en.R: But that very night {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Nathan a message. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said,

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came to Nathan: Yahweh gave him a message
decisions.reason: This is how the books describe a message given to a prophet (1 Samuel 15:10; 1 Kings 17:2). Verse 17 calls it a vision; it came at night.

decisions.choice: But that same night
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the verse to what comes before with a plain "and". Balanced and Readable say "But", because Yahweh's word overturns Nathan's quick approval.

source.text: לֵ֤ךְ וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ אֶל־עַבְדִּ֣י אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הַאַתָּ֛ה תִּבְנֶה־לִּ֥י בַ֖יִת לְשִׁבְתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Go and you will say to my servant, to David, Thus says Yahweh, [Is it] you [who] will build for me a house for my dwelling?

en.L: "Go and say to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave, to David, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Will you build {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to dwell in?
en.B: "Go and tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Are you the one to build {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house to live in?
en.R: "Go and tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Are you the one who will build a house for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to live in?

decisions.choice: my servant David: one who belongs to Yahweh and acts for him
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a slave, a person who belongs to a master. As a title from Yahweh it is an honor, given to Moses (Numbers 12:7) and to Joshua (Joshua 24:29). It marks David as the one who serves Yahweh as king, under his authority.

decisions.choice: Will you build me a house?: you are not the one to do it
decisions.reason: The question puts the word "you" first, and the answer it expects is no. The parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:4 says it outright: "You will not build me the house." Verse 13 names the one who will build it.

decisions.choice: a house for me to dwell in
decisions.reason: A temple was thought of as a god's dwelling. Yahweh does not refuse a house for his name (verse 13), but he will not be housed at David's wish; Solomon himself says that the heavens cannot contain him (1 Kings 8:27).

decisions.choice: my slave (Literal); my servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in the terms used for these books: Literal keeps the hard edge of the word, and Balanced and Readable say "servant", the usual sense of a title of honor (m1).

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); The LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The prophet's formula for introducing Yahweh's words keeps one wording at each level in these books.

source.text: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָשַׁ֨בְתִּי֙ בְּבַ֔יִת לְ֠מִיּוֹם הַעֲלֹתִ֞י אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וְעַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וָאֶֽהְיֶה֙ מִתְהַלֵּ֔ךְ בְּאֹ֖הֶל וּבְמִשְׁכָּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: For not I have dwelt in a house from [the] day I brought up [the] sons of Israel from Egypt, and until the day the this, and I have been going about in a tent and in a tabernacle.

en.L: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought up the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from Egypt until this day, but I have been moving about in a tent and in a tabernacle.
en.B: I have not lived in a house from the day I brought the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} up from Egypt until this day. I have been moving from place to place in a tent, in a tabernacle.
en.R: I have not lived in a house since the day I brought the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} up out of Egypt. All this time I have moved from place to place in a tent, the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: in a tent and in a tabernacle: in the portable sanctuary
decisions.reason: Both words name the one sanctuary made in the wilderness: "tent" for its covering and "tabernacle", which means dwelling place, for the place where Yahweh dwelt among his people (Exodus 26:1, 7; 40:34-35).

decisions.choice: I have been moving about: Yahweh went with his people
decisions.reason: The verb means to walk or go about. Yahweh used it in his promise to walk among Israel (Leviticus 26:12; Deuteronomy 23:15). He has never been fixed in one place, but has gone wherever his people went.

decisions.choice: until this day: through all Israel's history so far
decisions.reason: The sanctuary at Shiloh is called "the house of Yahweh" in 1 Samuel 1:7, 24 and had doors (1 Samuel 3:15), but it was still the tent sanctuary (Psalm 78:60). Yahweh's point is that he has never asked for a house to be built (verse 7).

decisions.choice: moving from place to place
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what Yahweh's "going about" means.

source.text: בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי֮ בְּכָל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ הֲדָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת־אַחַד֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֗יתִי לִרְע֛וֹת אֶת־עַמִּ֥י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֛מָּה לֹֽא־בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: In all where I have gone about among all [the] sons of Israel, [did] a word I speak with one of [the] tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, Why not have you built for me a house of cedars?

en.L: In all [places] where I have moved about among all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, did I speak a word with one of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, saying, "Why have you not built {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house of cedar?"'
en.B: Wherever I have moved about among all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, did I ever say a word to any of the tribes of Israel that I commanded to shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, asking, "Why have you not built {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house of cedar?"'
en.R: In all the places I went with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, I never said to any of Israel's tribes, whom I told to care for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel like a shepherd, "Why have you not built {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house made of cedar?"'

decisions.choice: tribes: the reading of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "one of the tribes of Israel". The parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:6 has "one of the judges of Israel", a word that differs by one letter. "Judges" fits the words that follow, "whom I commanded to shepherd my people", and verse 11 also speaks of judges. The word for "tribe" can also mean a staff or scepter, so it may stand here for those who held a ruler's staff. The translation keeps the Hebrew text; the sense in any case is Israel's leaders before David.

decisions.choice: to shepherd: to lead and care for
decisions.reason: Shepherding is a common picture of ruling a people: guiding, feeding and protecting them (5:2; Numbers 27:17).

decisions.choice: did I speak a word ...?: I never said this
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no: Yahweh never asked any of Israel's leaders for a house of cedar.

decisions.choice: I never said to any of Israel's tribes
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

source.text: וְ֠עַתָּה כֹּֽה־תֹאמַ֞ר לְעַבְדִּ֣י לְדָוִ֗ד כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲנִ֤י לְקַחְתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִן־הַנָּוֶ֔ה מֵאַחַ֖ר הַצֹּ֑אן לִֽהְי֣וֹת נָגִ֔יד עַל־עַמִּ֖י עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And now thus you will say to my servant, to David, Thus says Yahweh of hosts, I took you from the pasture, from after the flock, to be ruler over my people, over Israel.

en.L: And now, thus you shall say to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave, to David, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, over Israel.
en.B: Now then, say this to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.
en.R: So now, tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: I took you from the fields where you followed the sheep, and I made you leader of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

decisions.choice: Yahweh of hosts: Yahweh, commander of armies
decisions.reason: "Hosts" means armies: the armies of Israel and the powers of heaven, all under Yahweh's command (1 Samuel 1:3; 17:45).

decisions.choice: from the pasture, from following the flock
decisions.reason: David was a shepherd boy when Samuel anointed him (1 Samuel 16:11; 17:15, 34). Yahweh took the one who shepherded sheep to shepherd his people (verse 7; 5:2; Psalm 78:70-71).

decisions.choice: ruler: the leader Yahweh appoints over his people
decisions.reason: The word names a leader chosen by Yahweh to rule his people for him. It was used of Saul (1 Samuel 9:16; 10:1) and of David (1 Samuel 13:14; 25:30; 2 Samuel 5:2).

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (Literal); the LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in the terms used for these books. "Armies" says in today's English what "hosts" means.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: Readable says "leader" for the word for ruler, as in the terms used for these books.

source.text: וָאֶהְיֶ֣ה עִמְּךָ֗ בְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלַ֔כְתָּ וָאַכְרִ֥תָה אֶת־כָּל־אֹיְבֶ֖יךָ מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ וְעָשִׂ֤תִֽי לְךָ֙ שֵׁ֣ם גָּד֔וֹל כְּשֵׁ֥ם הַגְּדֹלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I have been with you in all where you went, and I cut off all your enemies from before you, and I will make for you a great name, like [the] name of the great [ones] who [are] on the earth.

en.L: And I have been with you wherever you went, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you, and I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great ones who [are] on the earth.
en.B: Wherever you have gone, I have been with you, and I have cut off all your enemies in front of you. Now I will make your name great, like the names of the greatest people on earth.
en.R: I have been with you everywhere you went. I have destroyed all your enemies as you faced them. Now I will make you famous, like the most famous people in the world.

decisions.choice: I have been, I have cut off ... and I will make: from what Yahweh has done to what he will do
alternatives: I have made for you a great name
decisions.reason: The first verbs tell what Yahweh has already done for David. With "and I will make" the verb form changes to the one used for the future, and the promises begin. Some read this verb and those in verses 10-11 as still telling the past ("I have made you a great name"), but the form and the promise in verse 11 favor the future.

decisions.choice: I will make for you a great name
decisions.reason: Yahweh made the same promise to Abram: "I will make your name great" (Genesis 12:2).

decisions.choice: cut off from before you: destroyed as they faced you
decisions.reason: Yahweh removed David's enemies one by one as David met them in battle (5:17-25; 1 Samuel 17:50).

decisions.choice: Now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "Now" to mark where the past ends and the promises begin (m1).

decisions.choice: make you famous
decisions.reason: Readable puts "a great name" in plain words.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י מָ֠קוֹם לְעַמִּ֨י לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וּנְטַעְתִּיו֙ וְשָׁכַ֣ן תַּחְתָּ֔יו וְלֹ֥א יִרְגַּ֖ז ע֑וֹד וְלֹֽא־יֹסִ֤יפוּ בְנֵֽי־עַוְלָה֙ לְעַנּוֹת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר בָּרִאשׁוֹנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will appoint a place for my people, for Israel, and I will plant it, and it will dwell in its place and not be disturbed again; and not will add sons of injustice to afflict it as at the first,

en.L: And I will appoint a place for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, for Israel, and I will plant it, and it will dwell in its own place and not be disturbed again; and the sons of wickedness will not again afflict it as at the first,
en.B: I will appoint a place for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel and plant them there, so that they may live in their own place and not be troubled anymore. Wicked people will no longer oppress them as they did at the beginning,
en.R: I will choose a place for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. I will plant them there like a tree, so that they can live in their own land and not be afraid anymore. Evil people will not hurt them again the way they did before.

decisions.choice: a place: a land where Israel can live in safety
decisions.reason: Here the place is the land where Yahweh will plant his people. The same word is used in Deuteronomy for the place Yahweh will choose for his name (Deuteronomy 12:5), and that may be heard here too, since a temple is being spoken of; but the words "plant" and "dwell" point to the land.

decisions.choice: I will plant it: settle Israel for good
decisions.reason: Moses' song says Yahweh would plant his people on the mountain of his inheritance (Exodus 15:17; compare Psalm 44:3; 80:9). A planted people is rooted and not moved again.

decisions.choice: sons of wickedness: violent, unjust people
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a quality means people marked by it. Here it means oppressors, like those who afflicted Israel in Egypt and in the time of the judges (verse 11).

decisions.choice: not be disturbed again ... as at the first
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into verse 11: "as at the first, and from the day I appointed judges". "At the first" is the oppression in Egypt; verse 11 adds the troubles of the time of the judges.

decisions.choice: plant them there like a tree; not be afraid
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture in "plant" plain and says what being "disturbed" means for a people: living in fear. It ends the sentence here, and verse 11 picks it up.

source.text: וּלְמִן־הַיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוִּ֤יתִי שֹֽׁפְטִים֙ עַל־עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַהֲנִיחֹ֥תִי לְךָ֖ מִכָּל־אֹיְבֶ֑יךָ וְהִגִּ֤יד לְךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּי־בַ֖יִת יַעֲשֶׂה־לְּךָ֥ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and from the day that I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will give rest to you from all your enemies. And declares to you Yahweh that a house will make for you Yahweh.

en.L: and from the day that I appointed judges over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} declares to you that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make a house for you.
en.B: ever since the time I set judges over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} declares to you that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make a house for you.
en.R: They did that from the time I put judges over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. But I will give you rest from all your enemies. And now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tells you that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make a house for you, a family of kings who will come after you.

decisions.choice: a house: a family line of kings
decisions.reason: Here the play on the word turns. David wanted to build Yahweh a house of cedar; Yahweh will make David a house of a different kind, a family of descendants who will sit on his throne (verse 16). The verb is "make", not "build" as in verse 5, though David will say "build" in verse 27.

decisions.choice: Yahweh declares to you that Yahweh will make: the oracle names the speaker
decisions.reason: Yahweh has been speaking as "I", but here the message names him twice by name. The change sets this promise apart as the center of the message.

decisions.choice: I will give you rest from all your enemies
decisions.reason: Verse 1 said that Yahweh had given David rest. Here it is promised for the time to come: the rest he has will last. Those who read verses 9-11 as telling the past read it "I have given you rest" (see verse 9).

decisions.choice: judges: Israel's leaders before the kings
decisions.reason: The judges were the leaders Yahweh raised up to rescue Israel from its enemies, from after Joshua to Samuel (Judges 2:16-18; 1 Samuel 7:15).

decisions.choice: a house, a family of kings who will come after you
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "house" for the play on it and adds what it means here (m1).

decisions.choice: They did that from the time
decisions.reason: Readable ended verse 10 with a full stop, so it starts a new sentence here that links back to the oppression.

source.text: כִּ֣י׀יִמְלְא֣וּ יָמֶ֗יךָ וְשָֽׁכַבְתָּ֙ אֶת־אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲקִימֹתִ֤י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֙ אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵצֵ֖א מִמֵּעֶ֑יךָ וַהֲכִינֹתִ֖י אֶת־מַמְלַכְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: When are full your days and you lie down with your fathers, and I will raise up your seed after you, who will come out from your inward parts, and I will establish his kingdom.

en.L: When your days are full and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, who will come out from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
en.B: When your days are complete and you rest with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, one who will come from your own body, and I will make his kingdom firm.
en.R: When your life is over and you die, I will make one of your own sons king after you. I will make his kingdom strong.

decisions.choice: your days are full and you lie down with your fathers: you die
decisions.reason: "To lie down with one's fathers" is the usual way these books speak of a king's death (1 Kings 2:10; 11:43).

decisions.choice: your offspring: first one son, and through him a line
decisions.reason: The word means seed, and so offspring. It can mean one descendant or a whole line of them. Here it is first one son, who will build the house (verse 13) and whom Yahweh will correct (verse 14): Solomon, who applies these words to himself (1 Kings 5:19; 8:19-20). But the promise reaches on to the whole line that follows (verse 16).

decisions.choice: who will come out from your body
decisions.reason: Yahweh used the same words in his promise to Abram of a son not yet born (Genesis 15:4). Solomon too is not yet born; his birth is told in 12:24.

decisions.choice: I will raise up: bring forward and set in place
decisions.reason: The verb is used for Yahweh setting a leader in place for his people (Judges 2:16; 1 Samuel 2:35).

decisions.choice: rest with your ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the wording kept for this phrase in these books; Readable says simply "die".

decisions.choice: I will make one of your own sons king after you
decisions.reason: Readable names what the offspring is in this verse, a son, and what being raised up means for him, becoming king. Verse 16 carries the promise on to the whole line.

source.text: ה֥וּא יִבְנֶה־בַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִ֑י וְכֹנַנְתִּ֛י אֶת־כִּסֵּ֥א מַמְלַכְתּ֖וֹ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: He will build a house for my name, and I will establish [the] throne of his kingdom until forever.

en.L: He will build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
en.B: He is the one who will build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I will make the throne of his kingdom firm forever.
en.R: He is the one who will build a house to be a temple that honors {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. And I will make sure that his throne as king will last forever.

decisions.choice: he will build: he, not you
decisions.reason: The word "he" is stressed, answering verse 5: David will not build the house, but his son will (1 Kings 5:17-19; 8:18-19). 1 Chronicles 22:8 gives the reason as David's many wars.

decisions.choice: a house for my name: a temple where Yahweh makes himself known
decisions.reason: Yahweh's name stands for himself as he is known and called on. Deuteronomy speaks of the place he would choose "to put his name there" (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11), and Solomon prays that his eyes would be on the house of which he said, "My name will be there" (1 Kings 8:29). Yahweh is present there without being housed there (verse 5).

decisions.choice: forever: for all time to come
decisions.reason: The phrase looks to a time without a set end. The word comes again and again in the chapter (verses 16, 24, 25, 26, 29). When the line of kings was broken at the exile, the prophets and psalms held to this promise (Psalm 89:30, 37-38; Jeremiah 33:17), and the New Testament sees it kept in Jesus, the son of David (Luke 1:32-33).

decisions.choice: a house to be a temple
decisions.reason: Readable says that this house is a temple, keeping the word "house" for the play on it.

source.text: אֲנִי֙ אֶהְיֶה־לּ֣וֹ לְאָ֔ב וְה֖וּא יִהְיֶה־לִּ֣י לְבֵ֑ן אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּהַ֣עֲוֺת֔וֹ וְהֹֽכַחְתִּיו֙ בְּשֵׁ֣בֶט אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וּבְנִגְעֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I will be to him for a father, and he will be to me for a son. Who when he does wrong, and I will correct him with [the] rod of men and with [the] blows of [the] sons of mankind.

en.L: I will be to him a father, and he will be to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a son. When he does wrong, I will correct him with the rod of {{gender:mortals|men}} and with the blows of {{gender:the children of mankind|the sons of men}}.
en.B: I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. When he does wrong, I will discipline him with a rod such as people use, with blows such as human beings give.
en.R: I will be his father, and he will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son. But if he does wrong, I will correct him. I will punish him the way people punish, with a rod and with beatings.

decisions.choice: I will be his father, and he will be my son: a bond of covenant care and loyalty
decisions.reason: Yahweh takes David's son into a relation like that of father and son: Yahweh will care for him, guide him and correct him, and the king is to honor and obey him and rule for him. The psalms use the same words of the king of David's line (Psalm 2:7; 89:27-28).

decisions.choice: Hebrews 1:5 quotes these words of the Son
decisions.reason: Hebrews 1:5 quotes the first half of this verse, together with Psalm 2:7, as words spoken of Jesus as the Son. In their first setting they are said of the son of David who will build the temple, and the next words expect that he may do wrong. Hebrews reads the promise to David's line as finding its fullest meaning in Jesus, the descendant of David.

decisions.choice: when he does wrong: the son may sin
decisions.reason: The promise does not say the son will be without fault; it says what Yahweh will do when he does wrong. The parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:13 does not have these words about wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: I will correct him: discipline him as a father does
decisions.reason: The verb means to rebuke or correct, with the aim of putting right. Proverbs 3:12 uses it of the same picture: Yahweh corrects the one he loves, as a father the son he delights in.

decisions.choice: the rod of men, the blows of the sons of mankind: punishment of the kind people give
alternatives: punishment by means of human enemies
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean punishment that is real but measured, as human beings punish, not destruction. Yahweh may also use human enemies for it, as he later raised up enemies against Solomon (1 Kings 11:14, 23). Compare Psalm 89:31-34.

decisions.choice: the rod of mortals; the blows of the children of mankind
decisions.reason: The words mean human beings in general, so Literal offers the inclusive wording by default with the traditional "men" and "sons of men" as the setting. Balanced and Readable say "people" and "human beings".

source.text: וְחַסְדִּ֖י לֹא־יָס֣וּר מִמֶּ֑נּוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֲסִרֹ֨תִי֙ מֵעִ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲסִרֹ֖תִי מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And my steadfast love not will depart from him, as I removed [it] from with Saul, whom I removed from before you.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} steadfast love will not depart from him, as I took [it] away from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful love will not leave him, as I took it away from Saul, whom I removed to make way for you.
en.R: But I will never stop showing him {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful love. I will not take it away from him the way I took it from Saul, when I removed Saul to make room for you.

decisions.choice: my steadfast love: Yahweh's loyal, faithful love
decisions.reason: The word names love that keeps faith with a bond: kindness that does not let go (1 Samuel 20:14-15). Here Yahweh binds himself to David's son without condition: even when the son does wrong (verse 14), this love will not be withdrawn. Isaiah 55:3 calls it "the faithful love promised to David".

decisions.choice: as I took it from Saul, whom I removed
decisions.reason: The verb "turn aside, remove" recalls 1 Samuel 16:14, where the Spirit of Yahweh turned away from Saul, and 1 Samuel 15:23, 28, where Yahweh rejected him as king. David's son will be corrected, but not rejected as Saul was.

decisions.choice: will not depart from him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text says "my love will not depart from him"; the parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:13 and the old Greek translation have "I will not take my love away from him". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: whom I removed from before you: whom I put aside to make way for you
decisions.reason: Saul was removed so that David could take his place (1 Samuel 15:28).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in the terms used for these books and in Exodus 34:6.

source.text: וְנֶאְמַ֨ן בֵּיתְךָ֧ וּמַֽמְלַכְתְּךָ֛ עַד־עוֹלָ֖ם לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כִּֽסְאֲךָ֔ יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֖וֹן עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be made sure your house and your kingdom until forever before you; your throne will be established until forever.

en.L: And your house and your kingdom will be made sure forever before you; your throne will be established forever.'"
en.B: Your house and your kingdom will be secure forever before you; your throne will stand firm forever.'"
en.R: Your family line and your kingdom will be secure forever before you. Your throne will last forever.'"

decisions.choice: made sure: firm, reliable, lasting
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the root that gives "amen" and "faithful": something that can be relied on to stand. Abigail foresaw for David "a sure house" (1 Samuel 25:28), and Yahweh had promised a faithful priest the same (1 Samuel 2:35).

decisions.choice: your house: your royal line
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, the house is David's family of kings. Together with the kingdom and the throne, it is promised to last forever.

decisions.choice: before you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text says "before you", that is, in David's sight, as though he will see it stand. The old Greek translation and a few Hebrew manuscripts read "before me", in Yahweh's sight, which agrees with David's prayer, where his house is to stand "before you", that is, before Yahweh (verses 26, 29). The translation keeps the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: forever: an unconditional promise
decisions.reason: The promise to David does not depend on his sons' faithfulness: their sin will bring correction (verse 14), but the line and throne will remain. Later passages keep this hope alive after the kings had fallen (Psalm 89:30-38; Amos 9:11; Isaiah 9:6), and the New Testament announces Jesus as the one who receives David's throne forever (Luke 1:32-33).

decisions.choice: secure
decisions.reason: Balanced says "secure" for the word meaning made firm and reliable (m1); Readable keeps the same word.

decisions.choice: your family line
decisions.reason: Readable says what the house is here (m2).

source.text: כְּכֹל֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וּכְכֹ֖ל הַחִזָּי֣וֹן הַזֶּ֑ה כֵּ֛ן דִּבֶּ֥ר נָתָ֖ן אֶל־דָּוִֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: According to all the words the these and according to all the vision the this, so spoke Nathan to David.

en.L: According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
en.B: Nathan spoke to David in keeping with all these words and all this vision.
en.R: Nathan told David everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to him in this vision.

decisions.choice: vision: a revelation given by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word names a message seen or received from Yahweh. This one came at night (verse 4).

decisions.choice: so Nathan spoke: he passed on all of it
decisions.reason: Nathan told David everything, though it overturned his own word of approval (verse 3).

decisions.choice: everything the LORD had said to him
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker behind "these words".

source.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מִ֣י אָנֹכִ֞י אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ וּמִ֣י בֵיתִ֔י כִּ֥י הֲבִיאֹתַ֖נִי עַד־הֲלֹֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went King David and sat before Yahweh and said, Who [am] I, my Lord Yahweh, and who [is] my house, that you have brought me as far as here?

en.L: And King David went in and sat before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Who [am] I, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, and what [is] my house, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have brought me this far?
en.B: Then King David went in and sat down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, who am I, and what is my house, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have brought me as far as this?
en.R: Then King David went into the tent and sat down in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, who am I? And what is my family? Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought me this far?

decisions.choice: sat before Yahweh: in the tent where the ark was kept
decisions.reason: To be "before Yahweh" was to be in his presence at the sanctuary, here the tent David had set up for the ark in Jerusalem (6:17; verse 2). Sitting to pray is unusual; David sits as one at home in Yahweh's presence.

decisions.choice: my Lord Yahweh: the master to whom David belongs
decisions.reason: David joins the title "my Lord", used of a master, to the name Yahweh. The pair comes seven times in this prayer (verses 18, 19 twice, 20, 22, 28, 29), and it answers Yahweh's "my servant David" (verses 5, 8): David speaks as a servant to his master.

decisions.choice: Who am I ...?: I am not worthy of this
decisions.reason: The question is a way of saying how small one is before a great gift or task (1 Samuel 18:18; Exodus 3:11).

decisions.choice: my house: my family
decisions.reason: Here David's house is his family, not the palace. He has just heard that Yahweh will make it a house of kings (verse 11).

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: Where "Lord" stands before the divine name, the name is printed "GOD" so that it is not read "Lord LORD", as in the terms used for these books.

decisions.choice: went into the tent
decisions.reason: Readable says where David went (m1).

source.text: וַתִּקְטַן֩ ע֨וֹד זֹ֤את בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֛ר גַּ֥ם אֶל־בֵּֽית־עַבְדְּךָ֖ לְמֵֽרָח֑וֹק וְזֹ֛את תּוֹרַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And was small still this in your eyes, my Lord Yahweh, and you have spoken also about [the] house of your servant for from far; and this [is the] law of the man, my Lord Yahweh?

en.L: And yet this was small in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken also of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant's house for a distant [time]. And [is] this the custom of mankind, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}?
en.B: And as if this were too little in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have also spoken about the house of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant far into the future. Is this the way human beings deal with one another, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}?
en.R: And as if that were not enough, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have also made promises about my family for a long time to come. People do not treat one another like this, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}!

decisions.choice: this was small in your eyes: as if this were not enough for you
decisions.reason: What Yahweh has done for David already is great, yet to Yahweh it was a small thing, and he has added more.

decisions.choice: for a distant time: far into the future
decisions.reason: "From far" can speak of distance in space or time. Here it is the future: Yahweh has spoken of David's house in the generations to come.

decisions.choice: and this is the custom of humankind?: no person deals this way
alternatives: and this is instruction for humankind
may this be the rule for the people
decisions.reason: The words, literally "and this is the law (or instruction) of the man", are hard to understand. The translation takes them as a question of wonder: people do not treat one another with such generosity, yet Yahweh has treated David this way. Others read them as "this is instruction for humankind", a word about David's line that reaches all people, or as a wish, "may this be the rule for the people". The parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:17 has different words: "you have regarded me as a man of high rank".

decisions.choice: your servant: David himself
decisions.reason: Calling oneself "your servant" is a polite and humble way of saying "I" when speaking to a superior (1 Samuel 17:32). David uses it ten times in this prayer.

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

decisions.choice: your servant (Literal, Balanced); I, me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Calling oneself "your servant" is the polite form of address, which has "your servant" at every level in these books (1 Samuel 23:10-11), Literal included. David's prayer speaks of himself as "your servant" again and again, and Readable often says "I" or "me" instead, since the phrase is a polite way of saying "I" (verse 19).

decisions.choice: People do not treat one another like this!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies (m3).

source.text: וּמַה־יּוֹסִ֥יף דָּוִ֛ד ע֖וֹד לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֑יךָ וְאַתָּ֛ה יָדַ֥עְתָּ אֶֽת־עַבְדְּךָ֖ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And what will add David again to speak to you? And you, you know your servant, my Lord Yahweh.

en.L: And what more can David say to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}.
en.B: What more can David say to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? You know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}.
en.R: What more can I say to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? You know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: What more can David say?: David speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: David names himself, as a servant might before his master. The question means he has nothing to add: Yahweh's gift goes beyond words.

decisions.choice: you know your servant: you know me through and through
decisions.reason: To know a person can mean more than to be aware of him: to know him closely and to have chosen him (Genesis 18:19; Amos 3:2). David has no need to tell Yahweh who he is.

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

decisions.choice: your servant (every level)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: Readable says "I" for David's name, which in English would sound as if someone else were meant.

source.text: בַּעֲב֤וּר דְּבָֽרְךָ֙ וּֽכְלִבְּךָ֔ עָשִׂ֕יתָ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַגְּדוּלָּ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את לְהוֹדִ֖יעַ אֶת־עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For the sake of your word and according to your heart you have done all the greatness the this, to make known [to] your servant.

en.L: For the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word and according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} heart {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done all this greatness, to make [it] known to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.
en.B: For the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word and as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own heart chose, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done this great thing and made it known to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.
en.R: You have done this great thing because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise and because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wanted to. And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have told me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, about it.

decisions.choice: for the sake of your word: because you had promised
decisions.reason: Yahweh's word is the promise he had already given, from David's anointing on (1 Samuel 16:1, 12-13), and now spoken fully through Nathan. The parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:19 has "for the sake of your servant".

decisions.choice: according to your heart: as you yourself chose
decisions.reason: What Yahweh has done comes from his own will, not from anything David earned (compare 1 Samuel 13:14).

decisions.choice: this greatness: this great deed
decisions.reason: The word means greatness, and here a great thing done: the promise of a lasting house.

decisions.choice: your servant (every level)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

decisions.choice: your promise
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word was, a promise (m1).

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֥ן גָּדַ֖לְתָּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה כִּֽי־אֵ֣ין כָּמ֗וֹךָ וְאֵ֤ין אֱלֹהִים֙ זֽוּלָתֶ֔ךָ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ בְּאָזְנֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore you are great, my Lord Yahweh, for there is none like you, and there is no God except you, in all that we have heard with our ears.

en.L: Therefore {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are great, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, for there is none like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and there is no God besides {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
en.B: That is why {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are great, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}. There is no one like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and there is no God but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, as all we have heard with our own ears tells us.
en.R: So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are great, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}! No one is like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. There is no God except {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Everything we have ever heard tells us so.

decisions.choice: therefore: praise that follows from what Yahweh has done
decisions.reason: David turns from Yahweh's gift to Yahweh himself: because of what he has done, he is great.

decisions.choice: there is none like you, and no God except you
decisions.reason: David uses the words of Israel's basic confession (Deuteronomy 4:35, 39) and of Hannah's prayer (1 Samuel 2:2).

decisions.choice: all that we have heard with our ears: what has been told from generation to generation
decisions.reason: Israel knew Yahweh's deeds from what parents told their children (Psalm 44:2; Judges 6:13).

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

source.text: וּמִ֤י כְעַמְּךָ֙ כְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל גּ֥וֹי אֶחָ֖ד בָּאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלְכֽוּ־אֱ֠לֹהִים לִפְדּֽוֹת־ל֨וֹ לְעָ֜ם וְלָשׂ֧וּם ל֣וֹ שֵׁ֗ם וְלַעֲשׂ֨וֹת לָכֶ֜ם הַגְּדוּלָּ֤ה וְנֹֽרָאוֹת֙ לְאַרְצֶ֔ךָ מִפְּנֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּדִ֤יתָ לְּךָ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם גּוֹיִ֖ם וֵאלֹהָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And who [is] like your people, like Israel, one nation on the earth, whom went God to redeem for himself as a people, and to set for himself a name, and to do for you the greatness and awesome [things] for your land, from before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, nations and its gods?

en.L: And who [is] like {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, like Israel, one nation on the earth, whom God went to redeem for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} as a people, and to make a name for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, and to do for you great and awesome [things] for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} land, before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} from Egypt, [driving out] nations and their gods?
en.B: Who is there like {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel, the one nation on earth that God went to redeem as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people? He made a name for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} and did great and awesome things for them and for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} land, driving out nations and their gods before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} from Egypt.
en.R: There is no nation on earth like {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel! God went to set them free so that they would be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people. That made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name famous. You did great and amazing things for them and for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} land. You drove out other nations and their gods to make room for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set free from Egypt to be {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own.

decisions.choice: who is like your people ...?: Israel's unique story
decisions.reason: David echoes Moses: no other god ever went to take a nation for himself out of another nation, with signs and wonders, as Yahweh did for Israel in Egypt (Deuteronomy 4:7, 32-34; 33:29).

decisions.choice: redeem: set free from slavery
decisions.reason: The verb means to free someone by paying a price. It is used of Yahweh rescuing Israel from slavery in Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8; 9:26).

decisions.choice: God went: Israel's God, with a plural verb
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, which could also be read "gods went". But the words "for himself" and the whole verse show that Israel's God is meant; the parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:21 has the singular.

decisions.choice: for them, for your land, driving out nations and their gods
alternatives: to do great things for you (Israel)
nations and its gods (as the Hebrew stands)
decisions.reason: The end of the verse is hard to read as it stands. It says "to do for you (plural) greatness and awesome things for your land, from before your people ... nations and its gods". The parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:21 reads "by driving out nations from before your people", and the translation follows that sense, taking "for you" as Israel and "its gods" as the gods of the nations. The old Greek translation has "to drive out nations and tents".

decisions.choice: [driving out]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the verb the sentence lacks, from the parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:21 (m4).

decisions.choice: for them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "for them" for the plural "for you" that suddenly addresses Israel, and break the long question into shorter sentences.

records.literal_gloss: And you established for yourself your people Israel for you as a people until forever, and you, Yahweh, have become for them as God.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} established for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel to be a people for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have become their God.
en.B: You established {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people forever, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have become their God.
en.R: You made Israel {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people forever. And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, became their God.

decisions.choice: your people ... you have become their God: the covenant
decisions.reason: This is the covenant promise: "I will take you as my people, and I will be your God" (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12; Deuteronomy 29:12).

decisions.choice: you established: made firm
decisions.reason: It is the same verb used for David's kingdom and throne (verses 12, 13, 16) and his house (verse 26). Yahweh has made both Israel and David's line firm.

decisions.choice: LORD (when David speaks to him)
decisions.reason: When the divine name is used to address Yahweh it is printed "LORD" without "the".

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבַּ֤רְתָּ עַֽל־עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְעַל־בֵּית֔וֹ הָקֵ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם וַעֲשֵׂ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, Yahweh God, the word that you have spoken about your servant and about his house, confirm until forever, and do as you have spoken.

en.L: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, the word that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken concerning {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and concerning his house, confirm [it] forever, and do as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken.
en.B: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, the word {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and about his house, make it stand forever, and do as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said.
en.R: So now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, please keep forever the promise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made about me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and about my family. Do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said.

decisions.choice: confirm: make it stand
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something stand, and so to carry out a promise (1 Samuel 1:23; 1 Kings 2:4).

decisions.choice: do as you have spoken: prayer that holds Yahweh to his promise
decisions.reason: David asks only for what Yahweh has already promised. His prayer rests on Yahweh's word, not on his own wishes.

decisions.choice: the promise
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word here is: a promise.

decisions.choice: LORD God
decisions.reason: When the name is used to address Yahweh it is printed "LORD" without "the" (verse 24).

decisions.choice: your servant (every level)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

source.text: וְיִגְדַּ֨ל שִׁמְךָ֤ עַד־עוֹלָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֱלֹהִ֖ים עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבֵית֙ עַבְדְּךָ֣ דָוִ֔ד יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֖וֹן לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And may be great your name until forever, saying, Yahweh of hosts [is] God over Israel; and [the] house of your servant David will be established before you.

en.L: And may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be great forever, saying, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] God over Israel'; and the house of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant David will be established before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name will be great forever, and people will say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is God over Israel!' And {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant David's house will stand firm before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Then people will honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name forever. They will say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is the God of Israel!' And my family, the family of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant David, will stand firm in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence.

decisions.choice: may your name be great: a wish, with its result
decisions.reason: The verb expresses a wish, "may your name be great", and also the result of verse 25: when Yahweh keeps his word, his name will be honored.

decisions.choice: established: made firm
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 16. David's house stands firm "before" Yahweh, in his presence and under his care.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (Literal); the LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: your servant (every level)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

source.text: כִּֽי־אַתָּה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל גָּלִ֜יתָה אֶת־אֹ֤זֶן עַבְדְּךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בַּ֖יִת אֶבְנֶה־לָּ֑ךְ עַל־כֵּ֗ן מָצָ֤א עַבְדְּךָ֙ אֶת־לִבּ֔וֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלֶ֔יךָ אֶת־הַתְּפִלָּ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: For you, Yahweh of hosts, God of Israel, have uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, A house I will build for you; therefore has found your servant his heart to pray to you the prayer the this.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, God of Israel, have uncovered the ear of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, saying, 'I will build a house for you.' Therefore {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has found his heart to pray this prayer to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, have revealed this to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant: 'I will build a house for you.' That is why {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has found the courage to pray this prayer to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, God of Israel, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have told me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, 'I will build a house for you, a family of kings.' That is why I have been bold enough to pray this prayer to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: uncovered the ear: revealed
decisions.reason: To uncover someone's ear is to tell him something he did not know (1 Samuel 9:15; 20:2).

decisions.choice: I will build a house for you: the reversal of verse 5
decisions.reason: David wanted to build a house for Yahweh (verse 5); Yahweh builds one for David. David uses the word "build" for what Yahweh called making him a house (verse 11).

decisions.choice: found his heart: found courage
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of will and courage (1 Samuel 17:32). Yahweh's promise has given David the boldness to ask.

decisions.choice: your servant (every level)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

decisions.choice: LORD of hosts (Literal); LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, addressed to Yahweh without "the" (verse 24).

decisions.choice: a house, a family of kings
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, Readable adds what the house is.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אַתָּה־הוּא֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּדְבָרֶ֖יךָ יִהְי֣וּ אֱמֶ֑ת וַתְּדַבֵּר֙ אֶֽל־עַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶת־הַטּוֹבָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, my Lord Yahweh, you, he [is] the God, and your words are truth, and you have spoken to your servant the good [thing] the this.

en.L: And now, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words are truth, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken this good [thing] to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.
en.B: And now, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words are true, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have promised this good thing to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.
en.R: Now, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone are God, and what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say can be trusted. You have promised this good thing to me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

decisions.choice: you are God: you and no other
decisions.reason: The words, literally "you, he is the God", stress that Yahweh is the one true God (Deuteronomy 4:35; 1 Kings 18:39).

decisions.choice: truth: true and reliable
decisions.reason: The word means what is firm and can be trusted. Yahweh's words will prove true; what he promises he will do.

decisions.choice: this good thing: the promised blessing
decisions.reason: "Good" here is the good that Yahweh has promised: the lasting house (compare 1 Samuel 25:30).

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

decisions.choice: your servant (every level)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הוֹאֵל֙ וּבָרֵךְ֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית עַבְדְּךָ֔ לִהְי֥וֹת לְעוֹלָ֖ם לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֞ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתָּ וּמִבִּרְכָ֣תְךָ֔ יְבֹרַ֥ךְ בֵּֽית־עַבְדְּךָ֖ לְעוֹלָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And now, be willing and bless [the] house of your servant to be forever before you; for you, my Lord Yahweh, have spoken, and from your blessing will be blessed [the] house of your servant forever.

en.L: And now, be pleased to bless the house of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, so that it may be forever before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, have spoken, and with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blessing the house of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant will be blessed forever."
en.B: So now, be willing to bless the house of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, so that it may last before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever. For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, have spoken, and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blessing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant's house will be blessed forever."
en.R: So now, please bless my family, so that it will last forever in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence. {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have promised it. Because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bless it, my family will be blessed forever."

decisions.choice: be pleased: a polite request
decisions.reason: The verb means to be willing or to agree to do something. It is a respectful way to ask.

decisions.choice: will be blessed: confidence, not only a wish
alternatives: let the house of your servant be blessed forever
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as a wish, "let it be blessed", but after "you have spoken" it is best read as David's confidence: what Yahweh has promised will happen.

decisions.choice: bless ... blessing ... blessed: the prayer ends where the promise ended
decisions.reason: The word for blessing comes three times, and the prayer closes, like Nathan's message (verse 16), on David's house lasting forever.

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

decisions.choice: your servant (every level)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

decisions.choice: my family
decisions.reason: Readable says "my family" for "the house of your servant".
